justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift assumption from what I inferred to be a current price near 1,355–1,360, likely referencing gold (XAU/USD) given the price level. For the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the prevailing price with only slight upward bias, recognizing that short-term momentum in gold has generally been supported by safe-haven demand, dollar softness, and geopolitical uncertainty. At one week, I nudged the estimate marginally higher to 1,365, reflecting a continuation of the same supportive macro backdrop but acknowledging that intraweek volatility could easily absorb or reverse that move. At one month, the estimate of 1,375 incorporates a slow grind higher consistent with persistent inflationary expectations and central bank buying trends, though the magnitude of movement remains deliberately conservative given how much can change over 30 days.

The confidence interval widths were primarily shaped by the natural scaling of uncertainty across time horizons. At one day, the 90-point range (1,315–1,405) reflects intraday and overnight volatility — gold can move 1–2% on a single macro release or geopolitical headline. By one week, the range widens to 170 points, incorporating the possibility of multiple Federal Reserve speakers, economic data prints (CPI, payrolls, PMIs), and shifts in Treasury yields or the dollar index, all of which have historically driven sharp gold moves. At one month, the 390-point range reflects the compounding uncertainty of a full macro cycle — multiple central bank meetings, evolving geopolitical developments, and the possibility of positioning shifts by large institutional players.

The most significant tail risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include an unexpected Federal Reserve policy signal — either a surprise hawkish pivot that aggressively strengthens the dollar (pushing gold well below 1,315) or dovish capitulation that could send gold surging above 1,570 in the monthly window. A sudden escalation or de-escalation in major geopolitical conflicts could also produce outsized moves. On the downside, a sharp risk-on rally driven by strong economic data could see institutional money rotate out of gold rapidly. On the upside, a financial stability event — such as banking stress or a sovereign debt scare — could trigger safe-haven demand that overwhelms my upper bounds, particularly at the monthly horizon.
